title: The Christians of Najran
hookLine: a Christian delegation from Najran is received in the mosque in Medina, and prays there

cards: Visitors from Najran, far to the south, walk into the Prophet's mosque in Medina just after the afternoon prayer.

They are Christians, scholars and leaders of their community, dressed in fine robes, and they have come to talk with the Prophet about who Jesus is. They have come a long way, with real questions, and they are guests.
Then their own time of prayer comes, there in the mosque. What happens next is the story. Today: the Christians of Najran.

teach.b: The sirah of Ibn Ishaq tells it simply. The Christians of Najran stand up to pray, in their own way, inside the mosque.
And the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, tells the people around him: let them be. So they pray in the mosque of Medina, facing east. Hold that picture.
Guests of another faith, praying their own prayer, under the same roof, and the host telling everyone to leave them in peace. Then come the conversations, and they're real.
The two sides disagree about Jesus, honestly and at length. Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet and the Messiah; the Christians of Najran believe him to be the Son of God.
Tradition links verses of the Qur'an's third surah to this visit.

teach.h: A WORD COMMON TO US AND YOU.
teach.b: Among them is an invitation the Qur'an addresses to the People of the Scripture: come to a word that is common between us and you, to worship none but God. The talks don't end with everyone agreeing.

teach.h: A TRUSTED MAN SENT HOME WITH THEM.
teach.b: Sahih al-Bukhari records that the leaders of Najran made an agreement with the Prophet and went home, and they asked him to send a trustworthy man back with them.
He chose Abu Ubaydah, and called him the trustworthy one of this community.
So the story holds three things together. Real disagreement, stated plainly. Real hospitality, down to the place of prayer.
And a relationship that continues, with a trusted person sent along.

how: Muslims retell the visit of the Najran delegation from the sirah and the hadith, and the scene of the Christians praying in the Prophet's mosque is cited in conversations about hospitality between Muslims and Christians.

games.q: you're in the mosque. the visitors from Najran stand up to pray their own prayer, right there. what does the Prophet tell the people around him?
o: wait until the mosque is empty.
games.why: let them be. they prayed in the mosque of Medina, facing east.

practice: Bring to mind someone whose faith, or lack of one, is different from yours, a neighbor, a coworker, an in-law, and set down for a moment any urge to win the argument.
Picture them in your home or your place of worship, comfortable, doing what matters to them, and you saying: let them be. If you pray, you can ask Allah to make you a good host.

wordCard.voice: Najran, the town whose Christian delegation prayed in the Prophet's mosque in Medina, with his leave, and went home with an agreement. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Najran, the town in southern Arabia the delegation came from.

carryVoice: Your line: guests in the mosque. Disagreement and welcome can share a roof. See you tomorrow.
